name: Knot Lock
summary: A pattern lock where a copper rope ties the dots, snaps apart when wrong and lights up gold when right
about: A phone lock screen with a 3 by 3 pattern grid. A copper rope follows your finger like a rubber band, dots lean toward you and pop as they are tied, and skipped middle dots join in by themselves. A wrong pattern makes the grid shake and the rope fall apart in pieces; the right one sends a light along the rope, opens the padlock and lifts the lock screen off a home screen whose apps spring in.
how: Press on a dot and drag across the others, then let go. The demo pattern is a Z: the top row, a diagonal down to the bottom left, then the bottom row.
Get it wrong and the rope snaps and falls; after three wrong tries the grid rests for a few seconds with a countdown ring on the padlock.
Tap Demo pattern to see the Z traced faintly on the grid.
Once unlocked, press Lock on the dock to drop the lock screen back down.
Keyboard: Tab into the grid, move with the arrow keys, Space ties a dot, Enter tries the pattern, Backspace undoes and Escape clears.
